new_confirmed_findings.evidence: I Do T4-A preamble: «c1:features:v1 identifica el intento»; theory T4-A: «identifica la operación, no el intento».
new_confirmed_findings.problem: The practical demonstration reverses the section's correct definition of idempotency identity.
new_confirmed_findings.reader_failure: A learner can generate a new key for each retry attempt, which makes deduplication impossible.
new_confirmed_findings.minimal_repair: Replace «identifica el intento» with «identifica la operación lógica y se reutiliza en todos sus reintentos».

new_confirmed_findings.evidence: I Do T4-A why: «La key case:step:ver es estable entre deploys de lógica»; We Do T4-A-E2 says v3 is needed after a deploy to avoid collision with v2.
new_confirmed_findings.problem: The text does not distinguish the version of the original operation/intent from the version of the currently deployed code. Regenerating an idempotency key from the new deploy version can make a delayed retry look like a new operation.
new_confirmed_findings.reader_failure: A learner may break deduplication during deployment by changing the key for an old request.
new_confirmed_findings.minimal_repair: State that the intent/version stored with the original logical operation is reused on retries. A new key is created only for a genuinely new logical operation, not merely because code was redeployed.

new_confirmed_findings.evidence: You Do requirements require a reusable durable checkpoint; starter uses CKPT/APPLIED in RAM; portfolioNote says «si puedes, reinicia el proceso leyendo CKPT desde disco».
new_confirmed_findings.problem: The defining promotion gate (restart from durable state without duplicate effects) is downgraded to optional enrichment.
new_confirmed_findings.reader_failure: A learner can finish the project with in-memory state, see the same-process retry pass, and believe they demonstrated crash recovery.
new_confirmed_findings.minimal_repair: Make persistence + fresh-process reopen mandatory, provide a SQLite/atomic-file scaffold, and fail the project gate if restart/resume evidence is absent.

new_confirmed_findings.evidence: Self-check Q1 scores «Procesos» as the generic CPU-bound answer; Q2 scores «Colas infinitas y OOM» and explains «maxsize acota memoria».
new_confirmed_findings.problem: The assessment converts known conditional/incorrect simplifications into authoritative 'correct' answers.
new_confirmed_findings.reader_failure: Even a learner who noticed the caveats is rewarded for reproducing the oversimplified rule, reinforcing the misconception.
new_confirmed_findings.minimal_repair: Rewrite Q1 around the default GIL-enabled pure-Python case and runtime measurement; rewrite Q2 to say maxsize bounds item count/backlog and requires separate memory measurement.

cross_element_issues.problem: Theory says idempotency key identifies the operation, not the attempt; I Do says the opposite.
The section asks learners to reason about ProcessPool IPC but practice measures JSON text length and calls it the actual IPC blob.
Theory admits the token bucket is static/no-refill, yet practical titles and feedback continue to call it a rate limit and claim ban protection.
The learning outcome promises cancellation/timeouts/resource cleanup, but all practical evidence is numeric classification or boolean flags.
The section names observability, trace and privacy gates but repeatedly validates them with a single dict and self-declared flags.
Durable crash/restart is simultaneously mandatory, absent from the scaffold, and explicitly optional ('si puedes').
The scored self-check promotes known conditional/incorrect simplifications to authoritative answers.
A criterion called obligatory is worth 15%, while the public badge copy states a 70% threshold; a hard-gate implementation was not located in this pass.
Crawler snapshot shows 19h/1040h while main encodes 9h/491h.
